discovery: Discovery of superconductivity in organic molecular conductors and the establishment of organic charge-transfer salts as model systems for strongly correlated electrons

nominees.name: Denis Jérome
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire de Physique des Solides, CNRS / Université Paris-Saclay, Orsay, France

nominees.name: Gunzi Saito
nominees.affiliation: Toyota Physical and Chemical Research Institute; Professor Emeritus, Kyoto University, Japan

subfield: Condensed matter physics (strongly correlated electrons, organic superconductors)
motivation: In 1980 Jérome and Bechgaard discovered superconductivity under pressure in (TMTSF)2PF6. This was the first organic superconductor, and it followed Bechgaard's synthesis of the TMTSF salts. Saito then designed the BEDT-TTF-based κ-phase salts, raising transition temperatures above 10 K at ambient pressure. These discoveries created a new class of materials. Their soft lattices and narrow bands let chemical and physical pressure tune the ratio of correlation to bandwidth continuously. As a result, organic conductors became the cleanest experimental platform for the bandwidth-controlled Mott transition, unconventional superconductivity next to antiferromagnetism, one-dimensional non-Fermi-liquid physics, and the first candidate quantum spin liquids, such as κ-(ET)2Cu2(CN)3. Four decades of worldwide research on correlated electrons, including work on the cuprates and on moiré materials, rest on concepts that these molecular crystals tested first. Close collaboration between chemists and physicists opened this field, and it deserves recognition.
